A hanging balance · the sixth bench

The Galvanic Cell

A cell runs on a difference. Drag two metals onto the rack into the two beakers and the brass voltmeter swings to E°cell = E°(cathode) − E°(anode) — the gap between their standard potentials, nothing more. Electrons crawl the wire from the metal that dissolves to the metal that plates up; swap the beakers and the needle flips sign but keeps its size. Put the same metal on both sides and the needle sits dead at zero — proof it is the difference, not either metal, that drives the cell.

Nernst concentration dial
[anode ion] / [cathode ion] = 1 / 1 · Q = 1 · the reading is E°cell exactly
Place a metal in each beaker — drag a lozenge from the rack, or tab to one and press Enter.

The activity ladder

Every pair you measure leaves a mark. From the signs of those readings alone — never the raw numbers — this column rebuilds the order. About 7 well-chosen pairs span all eight.

Place two metals to record your first comparison. Each reading tells you only which of the two is the nobler — but stack enough of those, and the whole activity series falls out.

Its sibling bench: the Aufbau Staircase
Two ladders of the same metals. Here you rank them by activity (E°) — how badly each wants to give up electrons. Next door you rank them by Aufbau order — how their shells fill. Same elements, two different orderings; step across to compare.
